Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

I can swim · I can't drive · Can you…?
FormUseExample
+can + verbI can swim.
–can't + verbShe can't drive.
?Can + subject + verbCan you cook?
shortYes, I can. / No, I can't.Can you swim? — Yes, I can.
  • can / can't + verb (base, no -s, no to): I can swim. He can dance.
  • Negative: can't (cannot) + verb: I can't drive. She can't sing.
  • Question: Can + subject + verb: Can you cook? Can she sing?
  • Short answers: Yes, I can. / No, I can't. can also asks permission: Can I sit here?

→ Describing people (she has blue eyes) comes next.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: I swim → I CAN swim. Can never changes: she can swim — no -s, no 'to'.
  • ⚠ Умею плавать / жүзе аламын = can swim — never 'can TO swim' and never 'she can swimS'.

Stage 6 · Speaking

Your turn

Write two lines with can: I can … / I can't … .

When you finish, open the model answer and check yourself.

Model answer

I can swim and I can cook. I can speak two languages. But I can't drive and I can't draw. Can you swim?

Check yourself:

  • Did you use can and can't?
  • Is the verb in the base form (can swim, not can swims)?
  • Can you ask a question too (Can you…?)?
Talk to Sam. Answer with the words from this lesson.

Sam

Sam

Listen: “She can sings.” 🤔

Why

can + base verb (no -s): She can sing. He can swim. Not 'can sings'.

Sam

Feedback

Well done: you used can / can't for ability. Next time, say it out loud too.
